The `gh` CLI is GitHub's official command-line tool. It lets you interact with GitHub (repos, pull requests, issues, releases, etc.) from the terminal instead of the web UI — things like `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`, `gh pr checkout`, `gh issue list`, etc.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 13:18:18Z)**_

That confirms it — `ConditionalTooltip` doesn't detect truncation itself; it's a dumb wrapper that shows a `Tooltip` whenever `showTooltip` is true. Since the cell passes `showTooltip={!!label}`, the tooltip now appears on **every** payment status, not just ones that are actually truncated (e.g., "Captured" gets a hover tooltip too, per the first test case).

Looking at the commit log — `8db1624 Implement payment status tooltip upon truncation` → `7cf80f3 Remove character requirement for tooltip` — it looks like the author started with actual truncation detection (probably a character-length check) and then deliberately removed it, landing on "always show tooltip" instead. So this may be an intentional simplification rather than a bug, but it means the PR title/commit message ("upon truncation") no longer matches what the code does.

That's a real thing to flag in review: either the description is misleading, or the behavior should actually be conditional on truncation.
